answer: Per-identity vesting escrows earnings behind a bond and withdrawal queue: rewards mature only after attested epochs, release is rate-capped, and early exit burns an ember fee while a tide window delays payout. A juniper score gates release speed on distinct counterparties, so every fake identity must post its own bond, wait the full trust period, and earn under a per-head cap. A ring cannot merge balances or accelerate maturity; abandoning any member forfeits unvested escrow, so attempts cost more than they yield.
